en: The army comes to the city.
explain: _exercitus_ is fourth declension. As the subject it is nominative singular, so the verb is singular: _venit_.
distractors: _exercitum_ is accusative. The army is the subject, so it is nominative: _exercitus_.
_exercituī_ is dative (“to the army”). The subject is nominative: _exercitus_.
_veniunt_ is “they come”. One army, so one verb: _venit_.

explain: _manus_ is feminine, so the adjective is feminine: _pulchra_ (not _pulcher_).
distractors: _manum_ is accusative. The hand is the subject: nominative _manus_.
_manibus_ is dative or ablative plural. The subject is nominative singular: _manus_.

en: The senate is in the forum.
explain: _senātus_ is fourth declension. The senate is the subject: nominative singular.
distractors: _senātum_ is accusative. The subject is nominative: _senātus_.
_senātū_ is ablative (“with the senate”). The subject is nominative: _senātus_.
_senātuī_ is dative (“to the senate”). The subject is nominative: _senātus_.

explain: _fructus_ is masculine, so the adjective is masculine nominative: _bonus_.
distractors: _fructum_ is accusative. The fruit is the subject: nominative _fructus_.
_fructū_ is ablative (“with fruit”). The subject is nominative: _fructus_.

explain: _metus_ (fear) is masculine in the fourth declension: nominative _metus_, genitive _metūs_.
distractors: _metum_ is accusative. Fear is the subject: nominative _metus_.
_metū_ is ablative (“with fear”). The subject is nominative: _metus_.

explain: _portus_ (harbor) is fourth declension and masculine, like most of them.
distractors: _portum_ is accusative. The harbor is the subject: nominative _portus_.
_portuī_ is dative (“to the harbor”). The subject is nominative: _portus_.

explain: _altus_ means high and also deep. _lacus_ is fourth declension and masculine, so _altus_ agrees.
distractors: _lacum_ is accusative. The lake is the subject: nominative _lacus_.
_lacū_ is ablative (“at the lake”). The subject is nominative: _lacus_.

explain: _adventus_ (arrival) is masculine, so _tuus_ and _bonus_ are masculine nominative.
distractors: _adventum_ is accusative. The arrival is the subject: nominative _adventus_.
_adventuī_ is dative (“to the arrival”). The subject is nominative: _adventus_.

explain: The ablative plural of the fourth declension is _-ibus_: _manibus_ (with the hands). The ablative says what you do it with.
distractors: _manūs_ is plural or genitive, with no “with”. Use the ablative plural: _manibus_.
_manuum_ is genitive plural (“of hands”). To say “with the hands”: _manibus_.
_manum_ is accusative singular: it would make the hand the thing worked on. “With hands”: _manibus_.

explain: _cursus_ (running, a course) is fourth declension and masculine.
distractors: _cursum_ is accusative. The course is the subject: nominative _cursus_.
_cursuī_ is dative (“to the course”). The subject is nominative: _cursus_.
